title: Which expression is greater in each pair?
description: Two pairs of expressions are compared by first working out the value of each side. Keeko doubts the comparison and thinks the bigger first number always wins.
teaching_notes: One idea: to compare two expressions, find both values first and then compare the values. Watch for children who judge by the first number alone.

source: Compare 10 + 2 with 7 + 1, and 13 − 2 with 4 × 3, using <, > or =.
video_script.why: The child learns to compare two expressions through their values.
video_script.substitution: Find the value of each side, then compare the two values.
video_script.anchor: Two pairs of expressions to compare
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko looks only at the first number of each side, so thirteen minus two looks greater than four times three because thirteen is bigger than four.
video_script.payoff_line: Ten plus two is greater than seven plus one

final_answer.spoken: ten plus two is greater than seven plus one, and thirteen minus two is less than four times three

maths_rules: slip: 13 is bigger than 4, but 13 − 2 is less than 4 × 3
video_script.design: One idea: find both values, then compare. Assumes the four operations. Wrong idea: the bigger first number wins. The two pairs stay on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two pairs of expressions side by side with an empty box between each pair

marks.book: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.pairs: the two pairs appear with an empty box between each pair

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>Compare ten plus two with seven plus one, and thirteen minus two with four times three.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which side is greater in each pair?

beats.on_screen: the two pairs stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: two scales with an empty box between them; the signs < > = appear beside the scales

marks.values: each side of the scale shows a question mark for its value
marks.signs: the three signs light up one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='values'/>To compare two expressions, we first find the value of each side.
<bookmark mark='signs'/>Then we compare the two values, using the signs for greater than, less than or equal to.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, ten plus two and seven plus one, then thirteen minus two and four times three.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sign for each pair

marks.find: the words the sign for each pair are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to put the right sign in each pair.

marks.vals: the two values 12 and 8 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='vals'/>Step one, find the value of each side of the first pair. Ten plus two is twelve, and seven plus one is eight.

marks.cmp: the sign > is written between 12 and 8

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>Step two, compare the values. Twelve is more than eight, so ten plus two is the greater side.

marks.vals: the two values 11 and 12 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='vals'/>Step three, find the value of each side of the second pair. Thirteen minus two is eleven, and four times three is twelve.

marks.cmp: the sign < is written between 11 and 12

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>Step four, compare the values. Eleven is less than twelve, so thirteen minus two is the smaller side.

marks.ans: the two signs are placed in the empty boxes and the answer is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Ten plus two is greater than seven plus one. Thirteen minus two is less than four times three.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows: the bigger first number wins; 13 − 2 = 11 and 4 × 3 = 12 beside it; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: the values 11 and 12 appear and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the bigger first number wins, because thirteen is more than four.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But thirteen minus two is eleven, and four times three is twelve. The first number alone does not decide it.
